ticket.title: outfeed gate: Law 12 regression warnings from the telemetry baseline
acceptance_criteria:
SCOPE 2026-11-07, from the flight-recorder alignment recorded in plans/GB-243.md section 12.3. First of four runtime consumers the spans unlock.

WHAT: when `outfeed gate` runs a step, compare its duration against the rolling baseline for that (repo, step) pair from `.gaugeblock/telemetry/index.sqlite`, and print an inline warning when it regresses plainly - the stated threshold is more than twice the rolling P50 and more than a 500 ms absolute delta (so a 3 ms step becoming 8 ms does not warn).

WHY THE THRESHOLDS ARE DOUBLE: a Law 12 warning that fires on noise teaches people to ignore warnings, which is worse than no warning. The absolute delta exists so tiny steps cannot trigger on ratio alone; the ratio exists so a genuinely slow step cannot hide under the absolute floor.

MINIMUM HISTORY, which is the part most likely to be skipped: a step with too few samples must say nothing rather than guess. "Too few" needs a written number (the design discussion suggests a rolling window and a minimum sample count) and the warning must print the sample count it used, so a reader can tell a baseline of 30 runs from a baseline of 3.

WHERE THE DATA COMES FROM: benchwork indexes spans into `.gaugeblock/telemetry/index.sqlite` (GB-243). A gate that reads that index couples itself to a file another process writes, so the read must tolerate a missing table, a database held open, and an empty window - each of those cases ends in "no warning", never in a failed gate. A performance advisory must never be able to fail a build.

NOTE ON AUTHORITY: law 12 requires that performance claims be measured. This ticket makes regression visible at the moment it happens rather than in a postmortem, which is the same law applied forward.

Done when: a deliberately slowed step warns with its sample count and the observed/P50 ratio, an unchanged step prints nothing, a gate run on a tree with no telemetry history behaves exactly as today, and none of those cases can fail the gate.
